summary: Phase 2 (HubSpot/Slack/n8n service-class + orchestrator) fully verified. Extended Phase 1 suite (27 tests) with a new /app/backend/tests/test_integrations.py (19 tests). Total 46/46 passed (100%). Verified: (a) GET /api/integrations/status returns all three providers with correct {configured,enabled,mode,last_sync,last_status,last_message} shape and mode='mock' by default; (b) POST /api/integrations/{hubspot|slack|n8n}/test returns status='mocked' when no creds; (c) invalid provider → 400; (d) INVALID hubspot token 'pat-na1-invalid-token-abcdef' triggers real HubSpot HTTP call and yields status='error' with 401 in the message; (e) fake Slack webhook (T00/B00/xxx) yields status='error'; (f) POST /api/leads emits full activity chain in strict order — created → qualified → email_generated → hubspot_contact → hubspot_company → hubspot_deal → slack_notified → slack_high_priority (score>=85), each with metadata {provider,action,status,data}; (g) after lead creation /api/integrations/status shows non-null last_sync for hubspot+slack, null for n8n; (h) GET /api/integrations/logs returns persisted logs with {id,owner_id,provider,action,status,message,lead_id,created_at}, provider filter works, owner isolation enforced; (i) POST /api/leads/{id}/retry-sync appends activities AND inserts new integration_logs; retry on lead with score=None → 400; retry on unknown id → 404; (j) PATCH /api/leads/{id}/status without hubspot token does NOT crash; (k) with auto_trigger_n8n=true + unreachable webhook (httpbin/status/503), n8n activity has attempts=3, status=error, elapsed >= 3s confirming exponential backoff (1s + 2s = 3s). Every Phase 2 class uses a FRESH signup user so parallel xdist workers cannot race on shared per-owner settings.

minor.issue: 'enabled' field reports Service.enabled which reads settings.auto_sync_hubspot / auto_notify_slack / auto_trigger_n8n. However n8n.enabled defaults to False and hubspot/slack default to True; documented, but consumers should note 'enabled' != 'will fire' — orchestrator.run_for_lead re-checks settings inline instead of using svc.enabled. Minor semantic redundancy.

activity 'message' is copied verbatim from provider result; when hubspot creates 3 objects (contact/company/deal) the mocked messages contain the lead email → PII exposure risk in logs. Acceptable for MVP; consider truncation/redaction before scale.

Only attempts hubspot sync when a hubspot contact_id can be found in prior activities. If the earlier hubspot_contact activity is mocked (no id), sync is silently skipped — this is the intended graceful behavior but there is no user-visible signal that the status wasn't synced upstream. Consider appending an informational activity.

critical_code_review_comments: services/n8n_service.py: BASE_BACKOFF*2**(attempt-1) sums to 1s+2s = 3s before final failure, matches request; but MAX_ATTEMPTS/BASE_BACKOFF env values live only in n8n_service — consider surfacing in status/logs so operators know retry policy without reading code.

services/orchestrator.py:run_for_lead runs 3 sequential HubSpot POSTs + optional deal-association PUTs; when auto_sync_hubspot=True with a real token this becomes 3-5 HTTP calls per lead in the request path. Consider offloading to a background task or aiohttp.gather where safe.

server.py:_extract_contact_id walks activities in reverse and returns the first hubspot create_contact id; if a retry-sync creates a NEW contact (409 → data.id is None), sync_status could target a stale contact. Acceptable for MVP but worth noting.

hubspot_service.py:create_contact/company/deal do not deduplicate — retry-sync will create duplicate HubSpot objects when a live token is configured. Consider searching by email/domain first or using HubSpot upsert.

hubspot_service.py:sync_status uses hs_lead_status property with SDR internal statuses ('contacted', 'converted'…) which are NOT valid HubSpot enum values by default. Real HubSpot calls will 400 unless the property is customized. Document setup requirement.

orchestrator._log: on Mongo insert failure the exception is only logged but the caller still receives a fully-formed activity dict → activities may claim 'success' with no persisted log. Consider bubbling up the persistence failure as a warning attached to the activity.

slack_service.py: fake webhook 'hooks.slack.com/services/T00/B00/xxx' currently returns 404 → status=error message like 'Slack HTTP 404: ...'. Good, but no distinguishing of 'invalid webhook' vs 'network hiccup' — could add 429 backoff.
models.py: Activity metadata is `dict` (untyped) — orchestrator writes {provider,action,status,attempts,data}; consider a Pydantic sub-model for stronger schema.

pytest.ini enforces -n 2 --dist loadscope; Phase 2 tests handle this correctly by allocating a fresh user per class, but any future test that mutates the demo user's settings will race — document this in a testing README.
test_credentials: demo@sdr.ai / demo1234 (existing). Phase 2 tests create their own TEST_* users per class for settings isolation.
seed_data_creation: Each Phase 2 test class signs up one throwaway TEST_* user in Mongo. Not cleaned up (preview DB, low volume). Leads are also left in place to keep integration_logs assertions valid.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full backend suite green. Run: cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://sdr-automation-2.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest tests/ -v. Total 46 tests, ~40s wall-clock (dominated by GPT-5.2 qualification calls). IMPORTANT: pytest.ini pins -n 2 loadscope; any new test that mutates /api/settings for a shared user WILL race across workers. Always sign up a fresh user via _new_user() (see test_integrations.py) for settings-mutating tests. The n8n retry test uses httpbin.org/status/503 as an intentionally-failing webhook; if httpbin is down replace with any URL that returns non-2xx quickly.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bugs found. During iteration two race-conditions surfaced from xdist parallelism (settings on demo user + separate motor loops); both were fixed by using fresh signup users and switching bare-Mongo teardown to synchronous pymongo.
